reason: Selected game experiments show capability-dependent gains and regressions from the complete refinement loop.

candidates.title: Check whether a model benefits from harness self-refinement
candidates.rule: Before enabling online harness refinement for an embodied agent, compare the full loop with a minimalist harness on the same target model, including completion and total inference cost.
candidates.passage: every Continual Harness variant on Flash-Lite underperforms the minimalist baseline.
candidates.finding: On Emerald, the Pro from-scratch condition reaches 100% of monitored milestones at a $130 median versus 98% at $215 for the minimalist baseline. Flash gains are variable; Flash-Lite refinement variants reach only 3–13% versus 20% for the minimalist harness.
models: Gemini Pro, Flash and Flash-Lite panel; inspected skill analysis identifies Gemini 3.1 Pro
workloads: Pokémon Red and Emerald embodied gameplay
candidates.conditions: Twenty-four-hour runs; the complete harness changes prompt, sub-agents, skills and memory online. The cost-completion comparison is reported on Emerald.
candidates.limitations: One game family and a combined intervention. Component effects and generalization to coding or business workflows are not established. In-game milestone progress is not proof of unbounded recursive improvement.
candidates.validation_test: For each deployed model, compare minimalist, fixed expert and refining harnesses over multiple seeds at matched spend and wall time; report completion, cost, regressions and variance.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
